title: Texcoco
capsule: Texcoco (Tetzcoco) was the principal Acolhua city-state on the eastern shore of Lake Texcoco in the Valley of Mexico, traditionally traced to Chichimec migrants under Xolotl in the twelfth century and serving as the Acolhua capital from the fourteenth century under a line of rulers including Quinatzin and Techotlalatzin. By the early fifteenth century it was the leading power of the eastern lakeshore, but in 1418 the Tepanec ruler Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco overthrew and killed its king Ixtlilxochitl I, subjecting Texcoco to Tepanec domination. Recovery came only at the very end of this period, when Ixtlilxochitl's son Nezahualcoyotl allied with the Mexica of Tenochtitlan to defeat the Tepanecs of Azcapotzalco around 1428.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Texcoco's core urban extent is documented archaeologically, and its political role in the Triple Alliance is detailed in multiple Indigenous and Spanish colonial sources; boundary demarcation of its tributary territory remains approximate.
